_comment: Settings > Graphics > Light and sky > Bounced light detail (2026-10-20; the Ambient level and probe streaming 2026-10-21). Each level is the two numbers the room light probes are laid out to (src/renderer/room_probes.rs lattice_for and Residency, docs/design/room-gi.md): spacing_m, how far apart every room's probes aim to be, in metres (a room that alone would hold more than a quarter of the level's probes coarsens by itself); and max_probes, the most probes held at once, by the rooms nearest the player, which is the size of the probe atlas. A room farther away shows one colour, worked out from its own lamps and windows, until it comes near. max_probes 0 is the Ambient level: no probes at all, every room its one colour, and spacing_m may be left out. Video memory is max_probes x 3,392 bytes (each probe's 10x10 light tile and 18x18 depth tile, 8 bytes a texel) plus 64,800 bytes for the row of room colours; the Settings page computes and shows it. The work each frame is about the same at every probe level (4,096 probes an update), so a finer level costs memory and takes longer to relight the rooms around the player. 'high' is the design (1 m, 32,768) and the default; src/config.rs falls back to it for an id not listed here. Values are clamped on load: spacing to 0.25 to 64 m, max_probes to what one atlas texture can hold (0 stays 0). Changing this file takes effect at the next start.

levels.name: Ambient
levels.note: One colour per room from its own lamps and windows: it follows the lamps and keeps rooms apart, but is flat within a room.

levels.name: Low
levels.note: Probes 2 m apart: soft, broad bounced light.

levels.name: Ultra
levels.note: Probes 0.75 m apart: the finest, and the nearby rooms finer too.
